claims.text: What the image looks like Buzzword: periarticular erosions, soft-tissue swelling, ulnar deviation on hand XR → RA
claims.quote: Periarticular erosions, soft-tissue swelling, ulnar deviation Hand X-ray Rheumatoid arthritis

claims.text: Radiographs show only soft-tissue swelling during the first months; subsequently periarticular osteoporosis, joint space (articular cartilage) narrowing, and marginal erosions may become visible; erosions often develop w.in the first yr but may occur any time
claims.quote: Radiographs show only soft-tissue swelling during the first months of disease. Subsequently, periarticular osteoporosis, joint space (articular cartilage) narrowing, and marginal erosions may become visible. Erosions often develop within the first year but may occur any time.

claims.text: US can detect synovial thickening and bone erosions, and synovitis and tenosynovitis w power Doppler; MRI = the most sensitive and detects early bony erosions
claims.quote: Ultrasound can detect synovial thickening and bone erosions. Synovitis and tenosynovitis can also be identified with ultrasound using power Doppler. MRI is the most sensitive and detects early bony a erosions.

claims.text: Ex aggressive early-RA hand radiograph: soft-tissue swelling of the metacarpophalangeal and prox interphalangeal joints, periarticular osteoporosis, symmetric joint space narrowing of several of these joints in both hands, and subtle erosions of third and fourth metacarpophalangeal joints
claims.quote: Features of aggressive, early rheumatoid arthritis, as seen in this radiograph of a 61-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis for 1 year, include evidence of soft-tissue swelling of the metacarpophalangeal and proximal interphalangeal joints, periarticular osteoporosis, symmetric joint space narrowing of several metacarpophalangeal and proximal interphalangeal joints of both hands, and subtle erosions of the right third and right and left fourth metacarpophalangeal joints.

claims.quote: This radiograph shows advanced, bilateral radiocarpal, ulnocarpal, intercarpal, carpometacarpal, and metacarpophalangeal joint space narrowing with associated chronic erosions, in addition to unrelated osteoarthritis.

claims.quote: This image of a patient with long-standing rheumatoid arthritis shows synovitis of the metacarpophalangeal joints with an ulnar drift of the digits.

claims.text: Aspects (abnorm in red) Virtually any joint, except the distal interphalangeal (DIP) joints, may be involved
claims.quote: However, virtually any joint, except the distal interphalangeal (DIP) joints, may be involved.

claims.text: Deformities: flex contractures may develop rapidly; ulnar deviation of the fingers w ulnar slippage of the extensor tendons off the metacarpophalangeal joints = typical, as are swan-neck deformities and boutonnière deformities
claims.quote: Fixed deformities, particularly flexion contractures, may develop rapidly; ulnar deviation of the fingers with an ulnar slippage of the extensor tendons off the metacarpophalangeal joints is typical, as are swan-neck deformities and boutonnière deformities.

claims.text: Sus w polyarticular, symmetric arthritis, particularly involving the wrists and second and third metacarpophalangeal joints; criteria incl RF, anti-CCP, and ESR or CRP; dx requires documented joint inflam and should ⍉be based on labs testing alone
claims.quote: Rheumatoid arthritis should be suspected in patients with polyarticular, symmetric arthritis, particularly if the wrists and second and third metacarpophalangeal joints are involved. Classification criteria serve as a guide to diagnose rheumatoid arthritis and are helpful in defining standardized treatment populations for study purposes. Criteria include laboratory test results for RF, anti-CCP, and ESR or CRP (see table ). However, diagnosis requires documented joint inflammation and should not be based on laboratory testing alone.

claims.text: Eti A chronic systemic autoimmune dz primarily involving the joints; damage = mediated by cytokines, chemokines, and metalloproteases; periph joints (eg, wrists, metacarpophalangeal joints) are symmetrically inflamed, leading to progress destruction of articular structures, USU w systemic Sx
claims.quote: Rheumatoid arthritis is a chronic systemic autoimmune disease that primarily involves the joints. Rheumatoid arthritis causes damage mediated by cytokines, chemokines, and metalloproteases. Characteristically, peripheral joints (eg, wrists, metacarpophalangeal joints) are symmetrically inflamed, leading to progressive destruction of articular structures, usually accompanied by systemic symptoms.

claims.text: Precise cause unknown; a genetic predisposition = localized to a shared epitope in the HLA-DRB1 locus; unknown or unconfirmed enviro factors (eg, viral infections, cigarette smoke) are thought to play a role
claims.quote: Although rheumatoid arthritis involves autoimmune reactions, the precise cause is unknown; many factors may contribute. A genetic predisposition has been identified and localized to a shared epitope in the HLA-DRB1 locus of class II histocompatibility antigens (1). Unknown or unconfirmed environmental factors (eg, viral infections, cigarette smoking) are thought to play a role in triggering and maintaining joint inflammation.

claims.text: Plasma cells prod antibodies (eg, RF, anti-CCP) that contribute to immune complexes, but destructive arthritis can occur in their absence; macrophages and lymphocytes prod pro-inflammatory cytokines and chemokines (eg, TNF-alpha, interleukins) in the synovium, and released mediators and enzymes contribute to cartilage and bone destruction
claims.quote: Prominent immunologic abnormalities include immune complexes produced by synovial lining cells and in inflamed blood vessels. Plasma cells produce antibodies (eg, rheumatoid factor [RF], anticyclic citrullinated peptide [anti-CCP] antibody) that contribute to these complexes, but destructive arthritis can occur in their absence. Macrophages also migrate to diseased synovium in early disease; increased macrophage-derived lining cells are prominent along with vessel inflammation. Lymphocytes that infiltrate the synovial tissue are primarily CD4+ T cells. Macrophages and lymphocytes produce pro-inflammatory cytokines and chemokines (eg, tumor necrosis factor [TNF]-alpha, granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor [GM-CSF], various interleukins, interferon-gamma) in the synovium. Released inflammatory mediators and various enzymes contribute to the systemic and joint manifestations of rheumatoid arthritis, including cartilage and bone destruction (1).

claims.text: Sx Joint Sx are characteristically symmetric; stiffness typically lasts > 60 minutes after rising in the Am but may occur after any prolonged inactivity (gelling); involved joints become tender and swollen, occasionally w erythema, warmth, and limitation of motion
claims.quote: Joint symptoms are characteristically symmetric. Typically, stiffness lasts > 60 minutes after rising in the morning but may occur after any prolonged inactivity (called gelling). Involved joints become tender and swollen, occasionally with erythema, warmth, and limitation of motion.

claims.text: Extra-articular findings can incl rheumatoid nodules, vasculitis (leg ulcers or multi mononeuropathy), pleural or pericardial effusions, pulm nodules, pulm infiltrates or fibrosis, pericarditis, myocarditis, lymphadenopathy, Felty syndrome, Sjögren syndrome, scleromalacia, and episcleritis
claims.quote: Extra-articular findings can include rheumatoid nodules, vasculitis causing leg ulcers or multiple mononeuropathy, pleural or pericardial effusions, pulmonary nodules, pulmonary infiltrates or fibrosis, pericarditis, myocarditis, lymphadenopathy, Felty syndrome, Sjögren syndrome, scleromalacia, and episcleritis.

claims.text: Tx and next step Goal: reduce inflam to prevent erosions, progress deformity, and loss of joint funct (a treat-to-target approach toward full remission or minimal dz activity has been suggested); DMARDs improve outcomes and are indicated for all pts
claims.quote: The goal is to reduce inflammation to prevent erosions, progressive deformity, and loss of joint function. A treat-to-target approach to achieve full disease remission or minimal disease activity has been suggested (1, 2). Disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs) have been shown to improve outcomes and are indicated for all patients.

claims.text: Tx almost all pts aggressively early, primarily w meds that modify dz activity
claims.quote: Treat almost all patients aggressively early, primarily with medications that modify disease activity.

claims.text: These incl conventional DMARDs (particularly MTX), bio agents such as TNF inhibitors, and targeted synthetic DMARDs such as tofacitinib
claims.quote: Medications that modify disease activity include conventional DMARDs (particularly methotrexate), biologic agents such as tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-inhibitors, and targeted synthetic DMARDs such as tofacitinib.

claims.text: NSAIDs may be used for analgesia but do ⍉prevent erosions or dz progression and may slightly increase cardiovasc risk, so their use should be limited; ↓dose systemic corticosteroids (prednisone < 7.5 mg Q1x day) may be added to control severe polyarticular Sx, USU w the obj of replace w a DMARD
claims.quote: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) may be used for analgesia, but they do not prevent erosions or disease progression and may slightly increase cardiovascular risk; therefore, their use should be limited. Low-dose systemic corticosteroids (prednisone < 7.5 mg once a day) may be added to control severe polyarticular symptoms, usually with the objective of replacement with a DMARD.
